reasons: Too few independent players for broad calibration.
Too few observations for calibration and held-out validation.
The estimator does not improve the held-out median-rating baseline by at least 10%.
Held-out mean absolute error exceeds 250 rating points.
The empirical uncertainty interval is wider than ±500 rating points.
Too few held-out observations across distinct rating bands.

model.target: Recorded Chess.com blitz rating, not ground-truth single-game performance

report.interpretation: Predicts recorded Chess.com blitz rating from move-quality similarity. Player rating is not ground-truth single-game performance. No Chess.com proprietary formula is inferred.
report.split: Player-hash folds 60/20/20. Train rows require both players in the train fold; calibration rows require a calibration player and no test opponent; test rows require a test player. No game can occur in two partitions.
limits: Pilot selection is one country inventory and one month
Features require 12 non-book unforced post-opening decisions and eight contested decisions
Engine profile is fixed; production reports with other budgets are unsupported
Repeated player observations are correlated; empirical interval coverage is not a formal population guarantee
Validation gates are prespecified engineering acceptance criteria, not a source-product calibration

sourceManifest.population: Chess.com public Italy country inventory of 10,000 recently active accounts
sourceManifest.selection: SHA256 ordering with salt rating-pilot-v1; first 60 country accounts, then up to39 SHA256-ordered one-hop opponents observed in selected games; at most four SHA256-ordered rated standard blitz games per account with 50–180 plies; duplicate game URLs removed
limitations: Recorded rating is a noisy player-level label, not observed single-game performance
Sample excludes short games and games longer than 180 plies
